## 🎯 Current scope and outcome

**Owner correction, chat 2026-11-03: BrowserStack phone runs stay in scope.** The earlier 2026-11-02 amendment meant there will be no *physical* devices, not that BrowserStack runs stop: “We should still be using browserstack the best we can to verify this. It's a real limit but we can burn it down. Monthly should cover android too.” The owner then chose to run three scopes on this PR before it lands: Safari authored acceptance, Android Chrome authored acceptance and Android Firefox tab acceptance. The record is the [2026-11-03 correction](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/blob/main/docs/implementation/SPN-090.md#correction--owner-chat-2026-11-03-browserstack-runs-stay-in-scope) in `docs/implementation/SPN-090.md`.

**⏳ Status:** none of the three scopes has passed yet. Each failure so far was diagnosed from the run's own report and screenshot and repaired. The scopes re-run one at a time on the final head, and this description records each result.

| Source identity | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Pushed head | See the PR's commit list; this round's repair sits on `2e266ed2bbc2ea0361797e6705236862d9cabb7f` |
| Earlier heads this round | `dab1d9d` (scope correction, monthly Android), `00ce6db` (first phone repairs), `7d348d6` (second phone repairs) and `2e266ed` (third phone repairs) |
| Last independently reviewed before this round | `076fdbc34afe2448fe503b0c9eb605efe9a9233a` (landing and desktop storage race) |
| Integrated main | `77cdd6c556c186cb5705b4d24e312da3aea36d3e` |

## 🔧 What changed since `076fdbc`

1. **📅 Monthly Android coverage (`dab1d9d`).** Three monthly crons (1st, 2nd and 3rd at 09:17 UTC) select Safari authored, Android Chrome authored and Android Firefox tab acceptance. Budget, admission, accounting and the displaced-run report follow the three-scope calendar.
2. **🗂️ Space pages prepare through Offline copies (`00ce6db`).** In a Space, Document actions offers **Offline copies**, not the Dashboard entry. A shared `browserstack-offline-preparation.ts` drives both flows. It waits up to 60 s for the result, fails on an alert and records the visible labels on a timeout.
3. **🦊 Downloads no longer wait for the storage answer (product change, owner's choice).** Firefox answers `navigator.storage.persist()` through its own prompt. The phone run cannot reach that prompt, and a person may ignore it. The run stayed on “Updating offline copy…”, which is consistent with the old code awaiting that answer before downloading (an inference: the label also shows while a download runs, so this re-run tells the two apart). The request now runs alongside the download. If the browser has not answered when the copy is ready, the result says it is still deciding and offers storage help, then shows the real answer. The answer is announced in all three result views. An open storage guide stays open, and the help button stays in place.
4. **📱 Chrome ⋮ menu in either spelling.** An en-GB phone says “Customise and control Google Chrome”. The resource-id fallback never matched the id Appium reports (`com.android.chrome:id/menu_button`), so `chromeMenuLabel` accepts both spellings and that id.
5. **🧭 Shared with me through the Browse files drawer.** At phone width the file places are only in that drawer. Every Shared with me visit in authored acceptance goes through `openSharedWithMe`.
6. **⏱️ Evidence inside the phase.** Each preparation wait leaves 20 s of its phase for the failure screenshot and label read, with a 1 s floor. `failureDiagnosis` keeps the screenshot first and the failed command as the lane's command.
7. **🧭 Safari navigates in the attached window (owner's choice).** On the iPhone every WebDriver `POST /url` took about 13.8 s (Chrome: 163–431 ms), which used up Safari's 240 s setup phase. Safari now opens setup items and every acceptance path with `location.assign` in the attached window, as Chrome already did for setup items. Chrome's acceptance paths stay on `POST /url`, which takes under 0.5 s there (owner's choice). The old page is marked before assigning, and navigation succeeds only once the URL matches and a new, unmarked document has loaded. Firefox keeps `POST /url`.
8. **📱 Chrome waits for Spinel after a relaunch.** `attach` waits up to 15 s for a window showing Spinel. It records each blank candidate, and the attempt count whether or not Spinel appears. Before, it read the contexts once.
9. **🦊 Worker state on a secure-worker failure.** If the page never gains a service-worker controller, the run records each registration's scope and worker states. This is failure-only evidence; the wait is unchanged.
10. **🧭 Safari's redundant input release (owner's choice).** After typing, the harness sends `DELETE /actions` to release anything held down. Every sequence already lifts its own finger and key, and Safari answers the release with `unknown command`. The harness now tolerates exactly that answer after a successful `POST /actions` and records it once. Any other error still fails.
11. **📱 Chrome offline reload before termination (owner's choice).** The relaunched Chrome window stayed blank for the whole 15 s wait, so item 8 did not help. Before the first time it closes the app, with the network already off, Chrome now reloads the open window once and records whether Spinel loads; the result is never required. If the attach wait still fails, the run records the page's scheme, Chrome's `ERR_…` code and the failed address's path, never the page text. This tells a Spinel offline defect from a Home Screen relaunch problem.
12. **🦊 Firefox waits for the network cut (owner's choice).** Firefox's socket still connected straight after BrowserStack applied `no-network`; Chrome and Safari were offline by then. At both no-network cuts, the harness now waits up to 15 s for both ordinary requests to fail before its single socket probe, inside the socket ticket's life, and records the attempts and the last probe. If they never fail, the run records that the cut did not reach Firefox. That the cut was merely slow is an inference; this record tests it.

Failed on the Space step, a harness defect (item 2). | [41733180670](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41733180670): stopped at the ⋮ menu on an en-GB phone, a harness defect (item 4). | [41748283045](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41748283045): the ⋮ repair held and Chrome reached the offline relaunch for the first time. The relaunched window was still blank when first read (item 8). | [41772261056](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41772261056): the relaunched window stayed blank for all 30 attempts in the 15 s wait, a white page with no origin; not timing (item 11). | ⏳ Pending |
| Android Firefox tab | [41708153615](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41708153615): readiness passed. The download never finished within 20 s; the cause was not yet known. | [41733934800](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41733934800): the menu read “Updating offline copy…”, consistent with the download waiting on the unanswered storage prompt (inferred; item 3). | [41749059341](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41749059341): at sign-in the page had no worker controller for the whole 15 s wait; earlier runs took about 3 s. Looks transient (inferred); a repeat records the worker state (item 9). | [41773348498](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41773348498): the worker controlled the page in 2.8 s, and sign-in and all four downloads passed. Just after the network cut the socket still connected (item 12). | ⏳ Pending |
| Safari authored | Not run | [41736478986](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41736478986): install, Home Screen launch, sign-in, four downloads, the Space page and the first cached folder passed. Failed on the hidden Shared with me button, a harness defect (item 5). | [41746157790](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41746157790): the Space page, the drawer, the offline relaunch and the Sheet reopen passed. The setup phase then hit 240 s on ~13.8 s navigations (item 7). | [41771504170](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41771504170): in-window navigation held (tens of ms each); every prerequisite passed in about 130 s and all four items reopened offline. Native editing stopped at the redundant release (item 10). | ⏳ Pending |

Each run's accounting and reconciliation completed. Every dispatch keeps the single account-wide lock, so the scopes run one at a time. The Chrome tab and Safari tab scopes stay label-only. The Firefox native-context HTTP 400 stays an accepted observation limit.

## ✅ Local validation (this round's candidate)

Under the serial watchdog with Node 26.12.1:

- `tsc -p .`, `oxlint --deny-warnings .`, `npm run format:check` and `git diff --check` passed.
- `node --test scripts/ci/*.test.ts`: 403 of 409 passed. The 6 failures are a known macOS `/private/var` vs `/var` temp-path mismatch in `doc-callback-sources` and `offline-upgrade-dependencies`, files this PR does not touch.
- `vitest run src/ui/offlineProtection.test.ts src/ui/deviceInventory.test.ts`: 70 of 70 passed.
- The new e2e case and story have not run locally; CI runs them.

## 🖼️ Visual review: “still deciding” result

Actual captures of the `ProtectionPending` story (`web/offline/OfflineAvailability.stories.tsx`), rendered by Playwright from local Storybook with the storage guide closed. Images are commit-pinned in `docs/implementation/evidence/`.

| Light, 1024×720 | Dark, 1024×720 | Phone, 390×844 |
|---|---|---|
| ![Light](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/blob/7d348d6a3d096cc322d6c0edcfb138764d4441de/docs/implementation/evidence/SPN-090-storage-deciding-light.png?raw=true) | ![Dark](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/blob/7d348d6a3d096cc322d6c0edcfb138764d4441de/docs/implementation/evidence/SPN-090-storage-deciding-dark.png?raw=true) | ![Phone](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/blob/7d348d6a3d096cc322d6c0edcfb138764d4441de/docs/implementation/evidence/SPN-090-storage-deciding-phone.png?raw=true) |

Captures show the resting state (no focus ring). An independent nonimplementing visual reviewer checked them against `docs/design/README.md`. Its first pass asked for changes: Done sat below the other actions, and the copy had an ambiguous “it”. After the fix it **approved**: one bottom-right action row, legible in both themes, no phone overflow. **Agent review only.**

## 🚦 Merge readiness

- [ ] Safari authored, Android Chrome authored and Android Firefox tab acceptance pass on the final head, each recorded above with its run ID and source.
- [ ] All seven required CI gates pass on the final head, including desktop Chrome.
- [ ] Two fresh independent nonimplementing reviews, each above 95, on the final head.
  - ⚠️ **Owner exception for this push (chat, 2026-11-03: "Re-review, then push").** No candidate can score above 95 before the phone scopes run. Round 37 graded `2e266ed` plus diff sha256 `36da5cbbcfd0969869a9152332c8710b8f2d54e533824bb379b3f747248109e2` (6 files), the tree committed as `62c1d20b26a19fbd32e9626bfbfe907ee076e7dc`. Reviewer S gave **87/100** and reviewer T **81/100**. Both approved the push and found no blocking defect; 8 and 12 of their deducted points were for the pending phone scopes.
  - Non-blocking notes:
    - S and T: the new wiring inside `runCapability` (the offline wait and the Chrome reload probe) is pinned by source matches; only the helpers are driven behaviourally.
    - S and T: a test comment says the probe runs "in every relaunch"; it runs before the first only.
    - S: a failed environment read after a successful reload would be recorded as a failed reload; a malformed network probe ends as `device-still-online` rather than as invalid (its last probe is kept).
    - T: the probe's worst case is about 30 s (reload, then a follow-up read), not 15 s; the blank-page field in `attach-attempts` skips the record sanitizer (it holds only bounded fields).
    - An earlier round (36) found the second no-network cut unguarded and the probe failing the lane on its own reload bound; both were fixed before round 37.
  - Merge still needs two reviews above 95 on the final head, after the phone scopes and CI pass.
- [x] Visual review of the new “still deciding” result: actual light, dark and phone captures, and an independent agent approval (**agent review only**).
- [ ] No unresolved blockers.
